# Private native Disable recovery qualification

This is an unformatted, uncompiled private source candidate. It is not an admitted
CI profile, production release, runtime result, full Next.js replacement, or a
claim that the framework is production mature. Native browser qualification and
all79 capabilities/11 release gates remain open. Both local Go caches are held,
preview3011 is protected, and AWS remains NO.

## Implemented source and authority

A single static platform bridge is prepended to the existing boot.js before Go
starts. Application state, routing and worker policy remain in Go. The bridge
captures33 DOM/SW native getter/method functions and finite preparation primitives
under trusted startup and continuing normal-platform semantics. It performs one
synchronous native ownership snapshot and exact native dispatch after the owned
Go authorization callback has linearized the exact cell/owner/operation/nonce.
There is no authored getter, Go/app callback, constructor, Promise observer or
await between final native facts and native dispatch. Only the initial parent
query fault is authored; every fresh first/final/child/retired-parent inventory
uses captured native methods and complete bounded native-field snapshots.

The exact parent record may still have empty worker slots. That is read-only
corroboration, never parent registration mutation authority. The parent native
controller must be exact, nonnull and owned. Child native registration inventory,
all slots/URLs and operation target must prove ownership; foreign overlaps,
duplicates, missing/partial/brand failures refuse. Successful native worker ACK
and native sender inclusion in the same controlled/visible pair couple the
actual parent to the actual target engine. Equal scope/script text does not
prove cross-partition object identity. Engine cap4 remains unchanged; the helper
is a real client with no exemption.

Fresh Disable status/control state is published only after a successful known
reply. Errored default false does not become confirmed Disabled. Native calls,
ports and callbacks are linked/charged before potential delivery; cancellation
cannot retry a destructive command or manufacture settlement. Actual native
unregister true/false/rejection and earlier successful Disable ACK remain distinct
partial outcomes. Success requires child native absence and a fresh parent-only
absence query after checked frame retirement. Native registry jobs are not CAS;
frame removal does not prove worker death, global job quiescence or client-ID
removal. Public serialized props/diagnostics remain browser-visible data.

Business entry and cleanup use different Go gates. Current authority/context is
needed for new business work. Original physical custody permits cleanup after
cancellation/controller replacement without granting new worker mutation or state
publication. Loaded helper cleanup, trusted-terminal unopened/CSP-denied cleanup,
and proved never-connected private node cleanup are separate modes. Retargeted,
moved, unknown-delivery or invalid native-identity state retains one quarantine;
no remove-as-abort or second helper attempt is allowed.

Missing DOM/SW/secure-context APIs or a failed capture/claim disable only offline
support. The bootstrap catches that optional failure locally; package init and
ordinary SSR/WASM/counter/navigation/core/module imports continue. No production
facet setter or map fallback exists. Unit map facets are explicitly TESTONLY.

## Continuing execution assumptions and current limits

The matched Go shim, native Promise/FrozenArray resolution and intrinsic transfer
semantics must remain ordinary during an operation. Hostile replacement of
Array.prototype.then/Object.prototype.then can alter native asynchronous query
resolution and is unsupported. No global freeze, prototype sandbox or pre/post
continuity proof is claimed. Instance/own worker.scriptURL getters removing or
retargeting a helper are still required reentry cases; final native reads bypass
them. Native WindowProxy/borrowed cross-realm getter acceptance must be measured
in actual supported browsers; missing/throwing native capability refuses.

Current callback counters prove Go handler-body completion, not return of the
outer JavaScript wrapper/native Promise reaction. Official Go permits releasing
a Func while it is running, so this is not by itself an unsafe Release claim.
No post-decrement child-native/property read was found in the current callback
tails. The stronger native-return/child-quiescence contract remains unqualified.
A separate parent-native callback-return prototype is being reviewed before
production integration; no default unit or compilation result may be relabeled
as that proof. The four specially tagged native Go witnesses remain explicitly
HELD and retain unresolved observer ownership rather than falsely claiming join.

Fresh UPDATE uses captured native queries and native update dispatch, preserving
the original normal query trace and allowing an owned waiting/installing slot
when active is null. Its old waiting/parent-status RPC physical seam remains
unqualified. Diagnostics preserve the real per-native UPDATE result while whole
coverage stays UNKNOWN; cleanupKnown is false once a legacy RPC is reached.
Actual frame listener/removal evidence remains mandatory. A denied helper before
any legacy RPC may report checked unopened cleanup separately.

## Same-production observations and browser cases

Read-only Go diagnostics copy one current-attempt scalar record from actual
bridge/cell/realm receipts. Unknown evidence is null/UNKNOWN, not zero. No native
refs, callbacks, nonce/requestID, capability, setter, ring, observer or extra
resource pool is exposed. The sample publishes a bounded envelope after the
public action returns, correlating an actual diagnostic admission revision with
its own completed-action revision. No advancement means unavailable rather than
reusing a prior attempt. Diagnostics do not replace confirmed business state.

Startup-native capture bypasses old post-startup prototype/channel/listener spies.
The reviewed fixture derivative therefore replaces that observation channel with
actual same-production receipts and independent real DOM/load/registry/cache
observations. It preserves16 declaration titles/intended outcomes, retry policy,
timeouts and worker/native boolean assertions; old immutable case bodies remain
archived. The first eight bodies, passive HTTP policy probe and raw native
cross-worker declaration remain byte-exact. UPDATE cases9/10 and private Disable
observation helpers are explicit derivatives, not silently identical witnesses.
One test document capture-load listener replaces old frame-own load observation;
it is cleaned on setup error and retirement. It is absent from production.

The prospective CORE profile selects all10 historical declarations plus five
current-generation declarations:60 cases across four existing projects. Genuine
legacy4 and helper-response-CSP4 are separate unadmitted profiles, never deleted,
skipped or marked passed by selection. Source configuration is not collection or
execution evidence. The ebb Firefox HTTP-policy test-probe failure remains a historical alternate
FAIL. Root's fresh3d core result is17PASS/1FirefoxFAIL/22UNRUN: the explicit
Disable page still rendered enabled=true with operation-error=conflict before
the Firefox policy case, which was unrun. Go source is identical across those
published revisions; no regression cause or private-source runtime fix is
inferred. The passive diagnostic and this unrun candidate supply no causal
production claim.

Private added cases exercise parent-empty native Disable, native parent frame-CSP
denial, actual three-user-document client cap success, over-four refusal without
false state, same-script uncontrolled target refusal, and genuine previous-worker
unsupported recovery without legacy replay. Native sender IDs, actual ACK/error,
unregister boolean, final registry, retained index/cache data and DOM/counter
identity remain real required observations. Persisted retained counts come from
the worker's actual snapshot; no helper subtraction or frame0-to-clientID claim.

## Deferred and unadmitted checks

Default Node-compatible JS unit roots and four future native-browser-tagged Go
roots have separate inventories. The native tag is
js && wasm && nextgo_native_browser && !nextgo_module; it is not selected or
qualified by default compilation. Missing native preconditions fail its future
profile; unresolved callback return deliberately keeps it HELD. Source fake
facets prove state-machine behavior only. No new browser declaration/case count
or source cap is admitted here. A bounded hosted Go1.24/1.27 first-compile/default
unit plan must use exact final pins, filters and root arrays under separate Root
review, without waiting for the held native profile to reveal compilation errors.

Genuine legacy qualification requires genuine immutable pre-recovery artifacts.
The unchanged optional body still uses the old strict two-binary index until a
separate reviewed A-only loader is deliberately composed. One A build cannot
satisfy two-index input. The dedicated genuine A-only producer/loader proposal is
separate and still held on finite timeout, whole-job disk, cold IO and transport
configuration gates. No fake old worker or unapproved AWS/network work is used.

Broader parity and maturity conclusions remain subject to their existing
implementation and qualification records. This private native recovery increment
does not close those release gates by itself.
